items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: I understand that my grandfather, John Glasgow, was half-Comanche Indian

ctx.x: Well, I always managed to get out of there quickly. I'd go as fast as I could, so I could get back and have time. Seemed like the evenings were long. I lived right near the school, and I'd get back home, maybe by 3:00. Five or ten minutes after three, and get out of my clothes and go to my grandmother's, maybe an hour later I'd be back, playing marbles with the rest of the guys. And some of the other games, you know.

But I did have a chance to sit and talk with her. I think -- although in later years, she told somebody in my family that some Indian man, and I understand that my grandfather, John Glasgow, was half-Comanche Indian, that she was rescued from -- they had a parade in San Antonio, Texas, and they were marching along there. Some Indians snatched her out of the parade, and the woman put her up under of her dress and kept her there. She was about 13 or 14 years old. Made her stand right there, and the police couldn't…
that kind of seems like it's a little bit out. but one of my sisters told me that she had told her that.
